title: Customer voice crib and experiment slate — May 2026
body:
TL;DR
Quick roll-up of the last 3 weeks of customer threads (support, sales calls, field notes). Pattern: lots of small, high-frequency asks about runtime observability and KV-cache visibility + several enterprise customers asking for predictable cold-start behavior and documented fallbacks. This doc is a scratchpad: prioritize small probes we can ship in 1–2 sprints, and one cross-team spike for cold-start SLA characterization.

Raw signals (top bullets)
- Recurrent ask: visibility into per-request (route/model) KV cache hits/evictions — customers want to understand cache efficiency and why latency spikes for certain prompts. (Seen in 7 accounts)
- Multiple users reported ambiguous "fallback to smaller model" behavior when Dedicated capacity is saturated — need clearer docs + telemetry. (2 enterprise deals flagged by AMs)
- A few teams observed embedded responses drifting after quantized model upgrade — ask for a sniff test + eval hooks before rollout.
- Latency anomalies: per-route 95th percentile spikes correlated with sequence-length extremes (long system prompts). Customers ask for guardrails / prompt-length SLO hints.

Clustered asks (quick map)
- Observability / Telemetry: KV cache metrics, per-token cost breakdown per request, cold-start trace for first token latency
- Predictable fallback behavior: explicit JSON field when fallback occurs, policy logs, explainability on which variant was chosen and why
- Rollout safety: pre-deploy embedding regressions detection, auto-rollback triggers (threshold-based)
- Guidance & docs: prompt-length best practices, batching trade-off cheat sheets for PLG users

Hypothesis & impact (1-3)
- H1: Increasing KV cache visibility will reduce repeat support tickets and churn risk for large embedding customers. Impact: medium-high (example: 2 customers >$10k/mo mentioned this as blocker).
- H2: Explicit fallback telemetry will reduce enterprise legal/security pushback when Dedicated bursts to hosted. Impact: high for sales enablement on multi-region accounts.

Proposed micro-experiments (ships in 1 sprint each)
1) kv-probe-001: Add per-request KV stats to the Console "trace" view (hits, misses, eviction count). UI note: collapsible details line in trace panel. Backend: expose counters in runtime trace. Owners: Marco (serving-runtime), Priya (console). Estimated effort: 3 dev-days + 1 test day. Risk: low. Linked: INF-987.
2) fallback-flag-quick: Add `fallback_reason` field to inference response when model variant fallback occurs + emit a routed event to audit log. Aim: quick safety for enterprise contracts. Owners: Liam (platform-eng), Marco. Effort: 4 dev-days. Risk: medium (routing mismatch edge-cases). Tickets: CS-2147.
3) prompt-slo-guidance: Short doc + banner in console showing "expected latency bands" per prompt-length and recommended batching configs. Owner: Evelyn (cs) + Docs. Effort: ~2 writer days + 1 UX day.
4) quant-check-run: Small evaluation harness to run embedding similarity checks before/after quantized rollout (smoke tests for 50 synthetic prompts). Owner: Applied ML. Effort: 2 dev-days + 1 research day.

Open questions / unknowns
- Runtime cost: how much telemetry volume will kv-probe-001 add? Need infra estimate (SRE/infra).
- Rollout semantics: how frequently do we emit fallback events — every request or sampled? GDPR/logging considerations for enterprise customers (security).
- Which customers want the KV detail in API vs just Console? Need a short survey from AMs.

Quick wins (can be assigned immediately)
- Add a line in public docs (hosted-api) about fallback behavior and sample JSON. Owner: Docs writer (Priya). Due: 2026-05-20.
- Create a short CS-runbook for talking to customers about cold starts (3 bullets + FAQ). Owner: Evelyn. Due: 2026-05-17.

Dependencies and blockers
- SRE: need cost estimate for additional metrics (open with infra). Contact: SRE on-call.
- Applied-ML: availability to run quant-check-run before next weekend.
- Legal: confirm retention policy for added fallback/audit logs for enterprise contracts.

Synthesis snippets (verbatim excerpts from calls)
- "We love the throughput but we can't explain the occasional 700ms spike — is our KV cache misconfigured?" — large embedding customer, May 5 call
- "If you silently route to a cheaper model during peak, we need to know — accounting and compliance require explicit notices." — security lead, finance company

Conversation threads to follow (links)
- Slack thread: #cs-voices — thread ts=165... (internal link in linked_artifacts)
- Confluence: voice-harvest-2026-05 (see linked_artifacts)
- GitHub PR: console/pull/432 (trace UI mock)

Next steps (this week)
- Monday: quick triage sync (CS + Marco + Liam + Docs) — confirm owners and surface any SRE red flags.
- Tue-Wed: Marco to prototype runtime trace schema (proto).
- Thu: Priya publishes fallback behavior doc + console banner mock.
- Fri: run a short AM survey to the 9 accounts flagged (quick 5-question Google form).

Notes to self (raw)
- Keep experiments small; this folder is for quick wins. If infra cost > small, escalate to exec for prioritized spend.
- Remember customers are usually satisfied if they can "see" the signals even when we don't fix the underlying root cause immediately. Visibility buys time.
- Follow up: capture two success metrics for each probe (ticket reduction, NPS lift, or sales momentum).

Appendix: rough impact scoring rubric (for quick prioritization)
- 1 (low) = affects <3 customers, mostly cosmetic
- 2 (medium) = affects ~3–10 customers, has measurable support lift
- 3 (high) = blocks deals or churn risk > $5k/mo

End of crib — leave comments below and I'll fold into a formal playbook if we get buy-in.

-- Evelyn
